extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, journal staff, and authors submitting biomedical research manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and guidance for completing and implementing the ICMJE uniform conflict-of-interest disclosure form for manuscripts submitted to biomedical journals; includes content, technical, and procedural recommendations. Intended to standardize reporting across journals and reduce confusion for authors and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a uniform electronic disclosure form
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE) developed an electronic uniform disclosure form and placed it in the public domain in October 2009.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to lessen confusion created by great variability in how different journals ask about and report authors’ potential conflicts of interest, and to ease the reporting burden on biomedical researchers. The form is intended for adoption by ICMJE member journals and encouraged for other journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on direct financial interests (direct exchange of money)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee believes competing interests are most clearly defined where they involve the direct exchange of money from an interested party to an individual author or the author’s institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This emphasis guided removal of some broader queries; the form still recognizes there are situations where indirect or nonfinancial factors could influence work, but the core definitional anchor is direct financial exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of queries about spouses and minor children
rubrics_metrics.description: The major change in the reporting instrument is the removal of the queries about potential competing interests of authors’ spouses and minor children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change was made on the basis of largely negative feedback and difficulty in defining competing interests beyond direct exchanges; removes a burdensome and unclear area of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of specific nonfinancial competing-interest queries and replacement with open-ended question
rubrics_metrics.description: Queries about nonfinancial competing interests were removed and replaced by a single open-ended query (new Section 4) asking, 'Are there any other relationships or activities that readers could perceive to influence, or that give the appearance of potentially influencing, what you wrote in the submitted work?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This places the onus on the person completing the form to identify and report appropriate nonfinancial competing interests; it is less intrusive than the previous specific questions while providing a locus to report perceived nonfinancial conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Onus on authors to report perceived nonfinancial conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: The revised form places the onus on the person completing the form to identify and report appropriate nonfinancial competing interests via the open-ended query.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to consider and disclose relationships or activities that readers could perceive to influence their work; this is intentionally less prescriptive than enumerating many nonfinancial categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeric designation of fields for clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Each field in the form now has a numeric designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change, together with modified language in the instructions and individual queries, was intended to improve clarity and usability of the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improved language and supporting glossary/translations for non-native speakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Language in the instructions and individual queries was modified; a glossary of terms used in the form and guidelines for translation into multiple languages are being created.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations must capture the essence of the queries rather than their literal meaning. The glossary and instructions will be posted on www.icmje.org and translations will be made available as they become ready to assist non-native English speakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical deployment requirement (Adobe Reader)
rubrics_metrics.description: To function, the electronic form requires the user to download the free Adobe Reader, version 8.0 or higher (Adobe Systems, San Jose, California).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a practical technical requirement noted as an issue raised during piloting; journals and authors should be aware of this dependency when deploying or completing the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional policy for authors who used older form
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who have completed the older version of the form in conjunction with a journal submission need not complete the new form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the new form will be the standard for new submissions going forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative community feedback and revision process
rubrics_metrics.description: ICMJE piloted the form, invited feedback from authors, editors, and other parties, and revised the form based on comments; the Committee welcomes continued input and will consider comments received before a stated deadline (comments considered before 1 May 2011 for the next iteration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form is intended to evolve in response to user feedback; journals and users are invited to send comments via the 'contact us' link at www.icmje.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for journals to adopt the revised form
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial encourages all journals to adopt the new version of the uniform disclosure form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption is intended to simplify and standardize reporting of conflicts of interest across journals, alleviating confusion and easing reporting burden on researchers so they can focus on research that improves care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pragmatic balance between burden and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgement that the complexity, subjectivity, and emotionality of conflict disclosure means opinions will differ about whether the vehicle is too burdensome or falls short in areas; 'We cannot, however, let the perfect be the enemy of the good.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The aim is to take a practical step toward simplifying and standardizing reporting rather than seeking a perfect but impractical instrument.
